interface_detail: The directory of gateways and the list of described Nym nodes are public JSON endpoints that answer with no credential; the exit addresses were read from the described-nodes list (exit_ipr) and the residential gateways from the dVPN directory. The vendor sells WireGuard dVPN and mixnet access.
tooling: Reading the exit list needs an HTTP client only. Using an exit needs the vendor client and an account; whether a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy endpoint exists was not established.
chaining: A free compute node runs the vendor client and the traffic leaves at one of the 80 exit addresses; the gateways are run by independent node operators, so the exit set is a pool and not one provider network.

limits.value: Up to 10 devices per account (mobile and desktop)

limits_note: Address concentration is a second constraint with no vocabulary kind: 80 exit addresses sit in 42 ASNs with the largest (AS200651 FlokiNET) holding 11; 50 of the 80 are on the datacenter list. Residential gateways are 37 of 623 listed gateways, 28 of the 37 inside one /24 (128.127.180.0/24, AS6696).
binding_note: What binds first is the ceiling attached to the account, 10 devices, not any byte quota, since the page states none.

identity_cost.detail: The 7-day trial is on select plans with a card and cannot be activated with cryptocurrency; paid plans list card, cryptocurrency, Apple Pay, Google Pay, GNU Taler and cash. unverified: what an account itself needs, behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: No suspension, throttle or data loss was measured. 50 of 80 exit addresses are in the datacenter list and 2 also in the VPN list, so a block met through one is datacenter-class; the 7 residential-classified gateway prefixes are a minority of the directory.
confidence_note: The list measurements are measured on 2026-11-03 from a registered classifier record; the plan facts are documented. The weakest rung is documented. Measured on the whole needs a live connection recording the address handed out, which was not done.
